sourceAssertions: HTTP admission never invokes the provider and rejects when no actual executor is registered.
All provider execution is entered through the dispatcher after a durable owner/epoch claim.
Heartbeat and owned terminal writes fence operation id, owner id, epoch, unexpired lease, and runtime profile identity.
The local signal and cancellation registry are optimizations; durable polling and cancellation metadata are authoritative.
An expired operation with provider-dispatch-started evidence becomes RecoveryRequired and is not reclaimed.
No production partial expansion or project-reference change was introduced.
behavioralCases: two independent service providers contend for one PostgreSQL lease
remote cancellation is observed by the current owner heartbeat
request disconnect after admission does not own execution cancellation
expired pre-dispatch work is reclaimed with a monotonically advanced epoch
available hosted dispatcher executes the exact admitted turn
terminal transitions release owner and lease timestamps
negativeCases: pre-SB04 request remains blocked behind provider execution
second live owner cannot claim the operation
missing local CTS cannot recover or abandon a live remote owner
expired post-dispatch evidence is never automatically redispatched
host without dispatcher cannot persist accepted work
profile/owner loss cannot fabricate a terminal result

acceptance.criterion: Only one instance can hold an execution lease for an operation at a time.
acceptance.evidence: Two independent providers share PostgreSQL and exactly one locked claim succeeds; owned writes also fence owner, epoch, and expiry.

acceptance.criterion: A client disconnect after admission does not cancel the durable operation.
acceptance.evidence: Real-host API returns 202 before provider release, request cancellation follows, and the durable operation still succeeds.

acceptance.criterion: Explicit cancellation reaches a local owner and is observed cross-instance within the configured bound.
acceptance.evidence: Cancellation is committed through a second context and observed by the owner's heartbeat adapter.

acceptance.criterion: Local registry absence never recovers or abandons another instance's live operation.
acceptance.evidence: Fake-time unit tests prove reconcile and abandon respect the durable live lease without a local registration.

acceptance.criterion: Expired pre-dispatch work may be reclaimed, while expired post-dispatch work becomes RecoveryRequired.
acceptance.evidence: Direct lease-owner tests advance the pre-dispatch epoch and fail closed after durable dispatch-start evidence.

acceptance.criterion: A host without an available dispatcher cannot falsely accept unexecutable work.
acceptance.evidence: Admission returns retryable DispatcherUnavailable and writes no operation when no executor registration exists.
